07. Data validation & limitations

What is confirmed, normalized, and not possible to conclude from these exports

Audit trail
Important discrepancy: In every month, summing the 1,000 Pages rows produces more clicks and impressions than the Chart total. No artificial adjustment has been made. Sitewide figures are shown from Chart; page, group and topic figures remain separate as reported. These two grains must not be reconciled by division or forced to match. Page coverage is not an estimate of search traffic share.
MonthGSC page rowsUnique bucketsChart clicksPage clicksΔ clicksChart impr.Page impr.Δ impr.Chart granularity

Normalization: removes query parameters, fragments, duplicate slashes, trailing-slash differences and case differences; treats /blog/slug/, /blogs/slug/ and the identical root-level slug as one article when mapped to a unique sitemap blog. Two calculator aliases are treated as likely migrations (/ovulation-calculator/ → /ovulation-calculator-free/; /bmi-calculator-for-women/ → /bmi-calculator/) and should be verified against the live redirects. Rows sharing the canonical path within a month are combined: clicks and impressions sum, CTR is recalculated, position is impression-weighted. Historical absence is never treated as zero. GSC position values were reported rounded by the source, so aggregated position is approximate. Months Jun–Sep contain one monthly Chart row; Jan–May contain daily rows. These exports alone cannot verify page response codes, canonical tags, actual redirect targets or full GSC page coverage.

Reporting: Sitewide KPIs are computed from Chart clicks, impressions and impression-weighted position. Topic, group, blog and row charts derive solely from the 1,000 monthly page rows. Blog classification uses matching sitemap category and exact-slug legacy aliases; some unlisted historical articles without a matching sitemap slug remain in “Other / unlisted pages.” This dashboard works offline and makes no third-party requests.
